text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- France would support Bulgaria's bids for membership in the European Union and NATO and would encourage French investment in the Balkan country, French President Jacques Chirac told visiting Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov.

-- Seven Western European countries would issue cheaper entry visas to Bulgarians or would abolish visa requirements for them in response to a recent decision of Bulgaria's interim cabinet to lift entry visa requirements for citizens of those countries, deputy Foreign minister Valentin Dobrev said.
-- Bulgarian customs officers said they had seized 43 kg of heroin early on Friday smuggled in a Polish-registered Mercedes mini-bus at the Kapitan Andreevo checkpoint on the border with Turkey. @

-- Two International Monetary Fund missions are expected to arrive in Bulgaria in the next two weeks to coordinate preparation for introduction of a restrictive fixed exchange rate mechanism, a currency board system, Bulgaria's Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would put into circulation a 50,000-lev note on May 8, the largest denomination to go in use so far. @

-- Bulgaria's insolvent Ocean Fishing company, in liquidation since 1994, might enter a consortium with three other companies ready to invest around $20 million in it, the government press centre said.

-- Interim Justice minister Haralambi Anchev rejected a proposal by the International Monetary Fund that local commercial banks were declared bankrupt by the Bulgarian National Bank and not by courts.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit fell by seven billion levs to 291 billion levs in the first half of April, Finance ministry figures showed.

-- Bulgaria and Hungary would hold the first round of bilateral negotiations for setting up a free trade zone between May 19-23 and talks on Bulgaria's bid to join the Central European Free Trade Area would be held simulataneously, Bulgaria's deputy Trade minister Minko Gerdzhikov said. @

-- Shareholders in state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank restored its one-tier management system by a board of directors to boost its operational flexibility, the bank's executive director Vladimir Vladimirov said.

-- Bulgaria's state-owned National Electricity Company (NEC) has accumulated some 38.8 billion levs in unpaid bills from customers as of March 31, NEC figures showed. The state radio, the state television, Bulgarian Railways and the Defence ministry were among the major debtors. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
